newsitem.title: SOUTH KOREA: S.Korean strike leader spearheads protest march.
newsitem.headline: S.Korean strike leader spearheads protest march.

text.p: South Korea's strike leader Kwon Young-kil left Seoul's Myongdong Cathedral on Wednesday and led a protest march through the streets, calling for the repeal of a controversial labour law, witnesses said.

For the first time since the law was rammed through parliament on December 26, Kwon and several deputies of the outlawed Korean Confederation of Trade Union left the cathedral where they had sought sanctuary from arrest.
There were no immediate reports of violence. The protest march came just one day after a stunning concession by President Kim Young-sam, who agreed to reopen parliamentary debate over the law.
As part of his climbdown Kim also said he would instruct officials to suspend arrest warrants served on Kwon and his deputies for organising more than three weeks of wildcat strikes.

Kwon, leading 4,000 protesters, was stopped by riot police ostensibly because the crowd carried a large banner which they did not report to police before receiving permission for the march. In South Korea all street demonstrations require prior approval from the authorities.
Kwon later returned to the cathedral, where the confederation has pitched a makeshift tent to house its strike headquarters.
